original_hook: When $MTL dropped 17.2% to $0.288, the sell-off wasn't a continuous wall of supply. Binance 1H klines show volume spiked to 582k units on the $0.320 breakdown bar and 501k on the $0.287 drop, then immediately collapsed to 72.7k units during the current $0.288 range. That 7x volume crash signals a forced liquidation sweep across thin order books rather than steady organic dumping. Once stop-loss clusters cleared, selling pressure vanished—but price remains pinned because spot buyers haven't stepped in. 📊 MTL 1H: price $0.288 • support $0.285 • resistance $0.35 • TP1 $0.26875 • target $0.2525 • SL / invalidation $0.35 (short bias). Levels are chart-derived scenarios, not guarantees. The catch. Low consolidation volume can also mean zero demand. If $0.285 fails on expanding volume, another liquidation leg opens up. What confirmation on $MTL would make you treat this setup as real rather than an early headline move?
